result.topic_en: Euler derives Theorem VI, which turns an alternating series with products in the denominators into a continued fraction, and applies it to e to obtain continued fractions for e/(e-1), 1/(e-1) and 1/(e-2).
result.transcription:
$\frac{1}{t} = \beta + \cfrac{\beta}{-1+\frac{1}{u}}$, $\frac{1}{u} = \gamma + \cfrac{\gamma}{-1+\frac{1}{v}}$, etc.
quare posterioribus valoribus in prioribus substitutis obtinebitur ista fractio continua:
$\frac{1}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha}{\beta - 1 + \cfrac{\beta}{\gamma - 1 + \cfrac{\gamma}{\delta - 1 + \text{etc.}}}}$
unde deducimus sequens Theorema.
Theorema VI.
§. 40. Si proposita fuerit huiusmodi series infinita
$s = \frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
exinde formari poterit haec fractio continua:
$\frac{1}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha}{\beta-1+\cfrac{\beta}{\gamma-1+\cfrac{\gamma}{\delta-1+\text{etc.}}}}$
§. 41. Si $e$ denotet numerum cuius logarithmus hyperbolicus est unitas, notum est esse
$\frac{1}{e} = 1 - \frac{1}{1} + \frac{1}{1.2} - \frac{1}{1.2.3} + \frac{1}{1.2.3.4} - \text{etc.}$ sive
$\frac{e-1}{e} = \frac{1}{1} - \frac{1}{1.2} + \frac{1}{1.2.3} - \frac{1}{1.2.3.4} + \text{etc.}$
Hic igitur fit $s = \frac{e-1}{e}$, tum vero
$\alpha = 1,\ \beta = 2,\ \gamma = 3,\ \delta = 4$, etc.
quare fractio continua hinc orinda est
$\frac{e}{e-1}$

$\frac{e}{e-1} = 1 + \cfrac{1}{1+\cfrac{2}{2+\cfrac{3}{3+\text{etc.}}}}$
§. 42. Cum igitur sit
$\cfrac{1}{1+\cfrac{2}{2+\cfrac{3}{3+\cfrac{4}{4+\text{etc.}}}}} = \frac{1}{e-1}$
haud difficulter autem demonstrari queat, si fuerit
$\cfrac{a}{a+\cfrac{b}{b+\cfrac{c}{c+\text{etc.}}}} = s$
tum fore
$a + \cfrac{a}{b+\cfrac{b}{c+\cfrac{c}{d+\text{etc.}}}} = \frac{s}{1-s}$
pro nostro casu erit
$s = \frac{1}{e-1}$, $a = 1,\ b = 2,\ c = 3$, etc.
quibus valoribus substitutis fiet
$1 + \cfrac{1}{2+\cfrac{2}{3+\cfrac{3}{4+\text{etc.}}}} = \frac{1}{e-2}$

items.quote:
Si proposita fuerit huiusmodi series infinita
$s = \frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{\alpha\beta} + \frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma} - \frac{1}{\alpha\beta\gamma\delta} + \text{etc.}$
exinde formari poterit haec fractio continua:
$\frac{1}{s} = \alpha + \cfrac{\alpha}{\beta-1+\cfrac{\beta}{\gamma-1+\cfrac{\gamma}{\delta-1+\text{etc.}}}}$
items.english: Theorem VI: if an infinite series of the form s = 1/α − 1/(αβ) + 1/(αβγ) − 1/(αβγδ) + etc. is given, then the following continued fraction can be formed from it: 1/s = α + α/(β − 1 + β/(γ − 1 + γ/(δ − 1 + etc.))).

items.quote:
haud difficulter autem demonstrari queat, si fuerit
$\cfrac{a}{a+\cfrac{b}{b+\cfrac{c}{c+\text{etc.}}}} = s$
tum fore
$a + \cfrac{a}{b+\cfrac{b}{c+\cfrac{c}{d+\text{etc.}}}} = \frac{s}{1-s}$
items.english: It can be shown without difficulty that if a/(a + b/(b + c/(c + etc.))) = s, then a + a/(b + b/(c + c/(d + etc.))) = s/(1 − s).
